facts.fact: The document says the Government of Ghana launched the electronic Integrated Criminal Justice Case Tracking System in 2018, for the Police Service, the Economic and Organised Crime Office, the Attorney-General's office, the Legal Aid Commission and the Prisons Service; it names no single owning ministry.

The document says the Ghana Case Tracking System project is being supported by USAID, whose Justice Sector Support Activity also pays for the awareness campaign; it gives no domestic budget line, and no date for the events, so the date is the document's published date.

systems.country_label: Ghana CTS; Integrated Criminal Justice Case Tracking System
systems.platform: integrated software with online, offline and Android versions
systems.owner: Government of Ghana, launched 2018; supported by USAID
systems.tiers: tracks criminal cases from arrest through investigation, prosecution, conviction and release across the Police Service, EOCO, the Attorney-General's office, the Legal Aid Commission and the Prisons Service; no count of stations given, and the campaign urges the public to demand that it is used at police stations

note: Governance facts only: the document describes what the system is for and says almost all personnel have been trained, but states no station, count or date of actual entry; the facilitator asks communities to demand its use at police stations.
